chunks: Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdullah b. al-Mughira and Muhammad b. Sinan, from Talha b. Zayd, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
He said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: There is nothing more corrupting to the heart than sin.
Indeed, the heart engages in sin, and it does not cease working upon it until it overcomes it, turning its bottom into its top and its top into its bottom.

key_terms.الخطيئة: Sin (khati'a), specifically referring to a deliberate transgression that corrupts the spiritual heart
key_terms.القلب: The heart (qalb), in Islamic thought the spiritual organ of perception, conscience, and connection to God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the effect of sin on the heart?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq quotes his father Imam al-Baqir's recurring teaching about the spiritual damage of sin. The imagery of the heart being 'flipped upside down' describes how persistent sin inverts a person's moral compass, making what was formerly recognized as wrong appear acceptable and vice versa. In Islamic spirituality, the heart (qalb) is the seat of spiritual perception, and this hadith warns that unchecked sin progressively blinds it.
